findings.title: ObservablesCache's own signature line omits history_depth, which its Arguments list documents
locations: PAGE: api / Cache, "The observables cache" signature: `ObservablesCache(domain; scalar = false, particle_velocities = nothing)`
PAGE: api / Cache, same docstring's Arguments list: "`history_depth = 1` — how many Lagrangian samples the run must be able to look back over…"
findings.contradicts: The docstring's own top-of-block call signature omits a keyword (history_depth) that the same docstring's Arguments section documents with a default and semantics.
findings.description: A reader who reads only the signature code-block (the normal way to look up a call template) will never learn history_depth exists, or that it must be set (e.g. to 4) to back an AdamsBashforth trajectory scheme. Signature and prose disagree within a single docstring.

findings.title: Architecture says one trajectory scheme exists; AdamsBashforth is fully built and wired
locations: PAGE: architecture §4.6: "the trajectory scheme — today the single second-order `EndpointHeun`, with higher-order schemes the studied future axis"
PAGE: api / Particles module docstring lists only `EndpointHeun`, omitting `AdamsBashforth`, `MultistepBuffers`, `restart!`, `history_depth`
PAGE: api / Particles, `AdamsBashforth(; order = 4)` fully documented as a shipped scheme
PAGE: api / SimulationRun, `Simulation` Arguments: "Pass `AdamsBashforth()` when trajectory accuracy in time limits a measurement"
PAGE: decisions: "(2026-08, user-requested) A second trajectory scheme: variable-step Adams–Bashforth"
findings.contradicts: Architecture §4.6's current-state claim that EndpointHeun is the only trajectory scheme, against the API pages and decision log showing AdamsBashforth as a second, front-door-selectable, fully documented scheme; the Particles module map (hand-written) also omits it while the auto-generated Index page lists it.
findings.description: Architecture prose was not updated after AdamsBashforth landed; the Particles module docstring's curated summary independently missed the same sweep, even though the auto-generated umbrella Index correctly lists AdamsBashforth, MultistepBuffers, restart!, and history_depth as current exports.

findings.title: Module include order stated two ways: Observables-before-State vs State-before-Observables
locations: PAGE: architecture §4.9: "SimulationDomain → Observables → State → Cache → Forcing → Generator → Propagator → Particles → SimulationRun"
PAGE: Home, "Components" ("listed in build order"): SimulationDomain, then State, then Observables, then Cache…
PAGE: api overview: "…build on one another in the order SimulationDomain → State → Observables → Cache → …"
PAGE: decisions: "The include order becomes State → Observables → Cache"
findings.contradicts: Architecture §4.9's layout summary (Observables before State) versus the Home page, the API overview page, and the decision log's own explicit sentence (State before Observables) — three independent surfaces agree against the architecture's current-state summary.
findings.description: §4.9 is a current-state section, not a historical log entry, so the disagreement is not covered by the append-only-log exemption; it is a live inconsistency about a basic structural fact.

findings.title: ConstantPower's band kernel: 'lazy, nothing stored' vs decision log's 'materialized indicator'
locations: PAGE: decisions, 2026-08 frame-compression entry: "`Linear` and `ConstantPower` keep one materialized real indicator each for the rate fill"
PAGE: api / Forcing, `ConstantPower` Fields: "`band` — the band-pass kernel, lazy… so no indicator array is stored"
findings.contradicts: The decision log states ConstantPower materializes a real indicator array; the Forcing API docstring states its band kernel is lazy and stores nothing — opposite residency claims for the same object.
findings.description: Linear's own Fields entry ('indicator — the band indicator as a real array') matches the decision log, so this is specific to ConstantPower's docstring disagreeing with the record, not a house-wide naming quirk.

findings.title: allocate_buffers's documented signatures omit the 3-argument form MultistepBuffers invokes
locations: PAGE: api / Propagator, `allocate_buffers`: only two signatures given — `allocate_buffers(scheme, domain; scalar = false)` and `allocate_buffers(scheme, tracers)`
PAGE: api / Particles, `MultistepBuffers`: "Build it with allocate_buffers(scheme, tracers, cache); a run builds it for you."
findings.contradicts: allocate_buffers's home docstring lists exactly two call forms; a third (three positional arguments, cache-taking) is referenced by name elsewhere and never listed at its own home.
findings.description: The same AdamsBashforth-landing documentation sweep gap as the trajectory-scheme finding, but a distinct failure mode: a signature omission at the one place (the generic's home docstring) that is supposed to enumerate every method.

findings.title: 'Uniform-mean-gradient scalar mixing' named as a built System with no visible implementing mechanism
locations: PAGE: architecture §3: "The System: … forced homogeneous isotropic turbulence, freely decaying turbulence, uniform-mean-gradient scalar mixing, and (a deferred frame, §7) homogeneous shear."
findings.description: In the same sentence, homogeneous shear is explicitly flagged deferred with a §7 pointer; uniform-mean-gradient scalar mixing carries no such flag, reading as already available. No mean-gradient production term appears anywhere else (scalar_rhs! is only advection + diffusion + forcing source; FlowConditions carries no gradient parameter; none of the five Forcing strategies mention one). If it is aspirational, it should carry the same deferred marker as homogeneous shear.

findings.title: "Today the single EndpointHeun" is stale — AdamsBashforth is a fully built, exported second trajectory scheme
locations: PAGE: architecture §4.6: "the trajectory scheme — today the single second-order `EndpointHeun`, with higher-order schemes the studied future axis"
PAGE: api / Particles, `AbstractParticleIntegrator`: "Two members today: `EndpointHeun` … and `AdamsBashforth`, a multistep method …"
PAGE: api / SimulationRun, `Simulation` Arguments: "Pass `AdamsBashforth``()` when trajectory accuracy in time limits a measurement"
PAGE: Home, Components: "Particles: Lagrangian tracer tracking — second-order advection … with a selectable interpolation scheme"
findings.contradicts: Architecture §4.6 says 'today the single second-order EndpointHeun … the studied future axis' while the Particles API page says, using the same word, 'Two members today: EndpointHeun … and AdamsBashforth' — a fully exported, order-configurable (default order=4) scheme with its own MultistepBuffers and cache-backed sample history.
findings.description: Architecture.md is the package's authoritative current-state spec, but §4.6 describes only one trajectory scheme as present and a second as future work, while AdamsBashforth is already built, exported (appears in the GBGIsotropicTurbulence Index), documented with its own type page, and wired as a `Simulation` front-door keyword. The Home page and API overview repeat the same incomplete framing. A reader would materially misjudge the package's current Lagrangian-tracking capability.
findings.resolution_hint: Update Architecture §4.6 (and the Home/API-overview one-liners) to name both schemes now that AdamsBashforth has landed; move the 'studied future axis' framing to whatever is genuinely still deferred (e.g. even higher order, or inertial-particle multistep).

findings.title: ObservablesCache's printed signature omits history_depth, documented two lines below it
locations: PAGE: api / Cache, `ObservablesCache` signature: "ObservablesCache(domain; scalar = false, particle_velocities = nothing)"
PAGE: api / Cache, Arguments (same page): "`history_depth = 1` — how many Lagrangian samples the run must be able to look back over, including the current one."
findings.contradicts: The printed call signature shows only two keywords and no `kwargs...` ellipsis (unlike Simulation's constructor elsewhere in the manuscript, which explicitly uses `kwargs...` to flag an abbreviated list), yet the Arguments list immediately below documents a third keyword, `history_depth`, absent from that signature.
findings.description: Same-page, self-contained defect: the constructor block presents itself as complete, but a keyword needed to size the AdamsBashforth multistep sample history is missing from it. Almost certainly a doc surface the multistep-support commit missed sweeping.
findings.resolution_hint: Add `history_depth = 1` to the printed signature block.

findings.title: allocate_buffers's documented method set is missing the three-argument (scheme, tracers, cache) form MultistepBuffers requires
locations: PAGE: api / Propagator, `allocate_buffers`: "allocate_buffers(scheme, domain; scalar = false) -> IntegratorBuffers / allocate_buffers(scheme, tracers) -> ParticleIntegratorBuffers" ... "One generic covers both because it is one concept"
PAGE: api / Particles, `MultistepBuffers`: "Build it with `allocate_buffers``(scheme, tracers, cache)`; a run builds it for you."
findings.contradicts: The home docstring for the generic allocate_buffers enumerates exactly two call forms and asserts 'one generic covers both,' but a third dispatch form (taking a cache argument) is used for AdamsBashforth's MultistepBuffers elsewhere in the same manuscript.
findings.description: Per the corpus's own 'one concept, one home' rule, every method of a generic belongs in its home docstring. A reader consulting the more central Propagator page for 'how do I allocate scheme buffers' would not learn a scheme like AdamsBashforth needs the cache passed too — the same undocumented-surface pattern as Findings 1-2.
findings.resolution_hint: Add the three-argument form to allocate_buffers's own docstring, or at least a forward pointer to MultistepBuffers.

findings.title: No documented verb populates the multistep sample history (particle_velocity_history) each iteration
locations: PAGE: api / Cache, `ObservablesCache` Fields: "particle_velocity_history — the earlier Lagrangian samples, most recent first ... history_filled says how many are valid."
PAGE: api / Cache, `deposit_sample!`: "Record the particle velocities already written into cache ... as current" (describes only the current-sample slot)
PAGE: api / Particles: record_particle_velocities!, advect!, restart! — none mentions pushing onto or shifting particle_velocity_history
findings.description: The cache clearly carries a rolling history for AdamsBashforth, and fields_modified!/particles_modified! are documented as discarding it, but no documented function is shown populating it iteration over iteration — a cold reader has to infer the update mechanism entirely.
findings.resolution_hint: State explicitly (likely in deposit_sample! or advance!'s docstring) which call shifts the history and appends the new sample.

findings.title: Home / API-overview one-liners still summarize Particles as strictly second-order, omitting the scheme choice entirely
locations: PAGE: Home, Components: "Particles: Lagrangian tracer tracking — second-order advection and field sampling along trajectories, with a selectable interpolation scheme."
PAGE: api, module list: "Particles: Lagrangian tracer tracking — Tracers, second-order advect! (Heun-in-time), and interpolate_at_particles! for the Lagrangian statistics."
findings.description: Map-level summaries that, unlike Architecture §4.6, don't literally say 'today the single scheme' — but still give no hint that a trajectory_scheme choice (EndpointHeun vs AdamsBashforth) exists at all, so a reader skimming only the front page would miss a documented, exported capability.
findings.resolution_hint: Mention the selectable trajectory scheme alongside the selectable interpolation scheme.

findings.title: VarianceController's default gain=1 sits at the low edge of its own cited O(1-10) range with no stated reason
locations: PAGE: api / Forcing, `VarianceController` Arguments: "gain = 1 — the dimensionless gain G. Larger relaxes faster; Bassenne report O(1-10)."
findings.description: Not a contradiction, but every other default choice in this corpus gets a one-clause justification (over's calibration argument, HouLi's machine-epsilon derivation); this one default sits at the extreme low end of a cited range with no stated reason for that placement, which may simply mirror the source paper's own default (undocumented either way).

findings.title: Module include order stated three different ways
locations: Architecture §4.9 'Layout summary': "SimulationDomain → Observables → State → Cache → Forcing → Generator → Propagator → Particles → SimulationRun."
api page (API overview): "the order SimulationDomain → State → Observables → Cache → Forcing → Generator → Propagator → Particles → SimulationRun"
Architecture decision log (2026-08, 'Observables precedes Cache'): "The include order becomes State → Observables → Cache"
findings.contradicts: Architecture §4.9 says Observables is included before State; the API overview page, the Home page's component list, the API index ordering, and the decision log's own dated entry narrating this exact reordering all say State before Observables.
findings.description: A basic architectural fact (module include order) is stated backwards in Architecture's own designated current-state 'Layout summary' relative to four other sources in the same manuscript, including the decision log entry that explicitly narrates the change to 'State → Observables'. §4.9 appears never to have been updated.

findings.title: Which call completes the particle-velocity deposit
locations: Architecture §4.6: "record_particle_velocities! records the new sample at the new positions from the same deposited field, completing the iteration's deposits"
api/Cache, deposit_sample!: "record_particle_velocities! writes, this call records ... since the write alone leaves the slot stale"
api/Particles, record_particle_velocities!: "it writes values only: the slot stays stale ... until deposit_sample! records them as current"
findings.contradicts: Architecture credits record_particle_velocities! alone with completing the iteration's deposits; the Cache and Particles API pages both state that record_particle_velocities! only writes and leaves the slot stale, and that the separate deposit_sample! call is what actually marks it current.
findings.description: A reader following Architecture's summary would believe one call suffices to close the particle-velocity deposit; the API docs for both modules that define the two verbs say a second call (deposit_sample!) is required or reads throw.

findings.title: Particles module docstring omits a whole scheme family and three exported names
locations: api/Particles module docstring: lists only Tracers, particle_positions, number_of_particles, AbstractParticleIntegrator, EndpointHeun, ParticleIntegratorBuffers, record_particle_velocities!, advect!, interpolate_at_particles!, new_vector_point_values, new_scalar_point_values
Same page later sections fully document AdamsBashforth, MultistepBuffers, history_depth, restart! — none named in the map
Architecture §4.7 also says only 'any Tracers with its own AbstractParticleIntegrator and ParticleIntegratorBuffers', silent on MultistepBuffers
findings.description: CLAUDE.md's own doc policy treats a module docstring as a map that must give 'a linked one-liner per operation', and states a capability list naming only a subset is stale even if literally true. Four of fifteen Particles exports — including the entire second trajectory scheme AdamsBashforth and its buffer type MultistepBuffers, added by a later decision — are missing from the module's own map; no other module docstring in the manuscript has this gap.

findings.title: allocate_buffers documented with two methods; a three-argument call used elsewhere
locations: api/Propagator, allocate_buffers: shows only allocate_buffers(scheme, domain; scalar=false) -> IntegratorBuffers and allocate_buffers(scheme, tracers) -> ParticleIntegratorBuffers
api/Particles, MultistepBuffers: "Build it with allocate_buffers(scheme, tracers, cache); a run builds it for you."
findings.contradicts: The generic's own docstring — the designated home for its signature — enumerates exactly two methods, neither taking a cache argument, while MultistepBuffers' docstring invokes an undocumented three-argument form.
findings.description: A reader consulting allocate_buffers to learn how to build any of its return types has no way to discover the three-argument overload needed for MultistepBuffers.

findings.title: ObservablesCache's printed constructor signature omits a keyword its own Arguments list documents
locations: api/Cache, ObservablesCache signature: "ObservablesCache(domain; scalar = false, particle_velocities = nothing)"
Same docstring, Arguments: "history_depth = 1 — how many Lagrangian samples the run must be able to look back over ..."
findings.contradicts: The code-block signature and the prose Arguments section of the same docstring disagree about which keywords the constructor accepts (two vs three).
findings.description: A reader who copies the printed signature would omit a real, separately documented keyword (history_depth) that a multistep trajectory scheme needs the cache built with.

findings.title: fields_modified! lacks the Simulation-argument form its declared twin particles_modified! has
locations: Architecture §4.1: "declared through fields_modified! — or ... through the particle-side twin particles_modified!"
api/Cache, fields_modified!: single signature fields_modified!(cache)
api/Cache, particles_modified!: two signatures, cache and sim, "mirroring deposit!'s two forms"
findings.contradicts: If the two announce-functions are twins and both mirror deposit! (which has both a cache and a sim form), fields_modified! would be expected to have the same sim convenience overload particles_modified! was explicitly given; it does not, and no page explains the asymmetry.
findings.description: May be deliberate, but nothing in the manuscript says so, and the explicit 'twin'/'mirroring' language invites an expectation of symmetry that is not delivered.

findings.title: ARCHITECTURE §4.6 says one trajectory scheme exists; the Particles page ships two
locations: PAGE: architecture, §4.6 — "the trajectory scheme — today the single second-order `EndpointHeun`, with higher-order schemes the studied future axis"
PAGE: api / Particles, `AbstractParticleIntegrator` — "Two members today: `EndpointHeun` … and `AdamsBashforth`"
PAGE: api overview, Particles — "second-order `advect!` (Heun-in-time)"
findings.contradicts: PAGE: api / Particles — "Two members today" — axis: how many trajectory schemes exist NOW (one vs two)
findings.description: §4.6 is a current-state section, not the append-only log, so this is stale rather than history. The staleness propagates: the api overview and Home page both describe particle tracking as second-order Heun only, though a variable-step Adams-Bashforth (order up to 8) is exported and offered by Simulation's `trajectory_scheme`. §4.6's `allocate_buffers(scheme, tracers)` is also incomplete — the multistep form takes the cache as a third argument.
findings.resolution_hint: Rewrite §4.6's "two axes matter" sentence around both shipped schemes and sweep the Home/api-overview one-liners in the same pass.

findings.title: "Four strategies are provided" — five are
locations: PAGE: architecture, §4.4 — "Four strategies are provided." then NoForcing, Linear, ConstantPower, VarianceController, VarianceRescaling
PAGE: architecture, §4.4 — "because these four methods are written through tensor-order-generic field operators"
PAGE: api / Forcing, module map — five bullets, `NoForcing` … `VarianceRescaling`
findings.contradicts: PAGE: api / Forcing module map (and Home page) list five strategies — axis: the count of built forcing strategies
findings.description: The count was correct before `VarianceController` became the default (decision 58) and was not swept. Both instances sit in one paragraph, and the second ("these four methods") is the sentence a reader uses to decide which strategies share one tensor-order-generic implementation.
findings.resolution_hint: Change both to five; check no other capability list stopped at the pre-controller menu.

findings.title: A fixed-injection forcing: does k ring, or random-walk with nothing to return it?
locations: PAGE: api / Forcing, `VarianceController` — "the variance random-walks with nothing to return it — which is what the rate-clamping forcings do"
PAGE: api / Observables, module — "a fixed-injection forcing makes it ring"
PAGE: api / Forcing, `ConstantPower` — "`injection_rate` is the value $\varepsilon$ relaxes to in the stationary mean"
findings.contradicts: PAGE: api / Observables — "a fixed-injection forcing makes it ring" — axis: whether a rate-holding forcing leaves k unrestored (random walk) or restored/oscillatory
findings.description: With injection held at P, dk/dt = P − ε(k) has a single attracting equilibrium reached through the cascade — exactly the "ring" and "relaxes to" the other two surfaces describe. "Every k an equilibrium, nothing to return it" holds for the bare marginal law A = ε/2k_f, which no shipped strategy uses; attributing it to "the rate-clamping forcings" reads as a claim about ConstantPower and mis-states its physics.
findings.resolution_hint: Keep the marginal-law sentence but name the bare ε-matching rate, not the shipped fixed-injection strategy.

findings.title: The large-eddy turnover time is defined two ways, a factor 3/2 apart
locations: PAGE: api / Forcing, `VarianceController` — "the large-eddy turnover time $t_\ell$. When omitted it is taken as $2k_\infty/3\varepsilon_\infty$"
PAGE: api / SimulationRun, `StationarityCriterion` — "the eddy-turnover clock $\Delta t \varepsilon/k$"
PAGE: observables_cache, §1.3 — "accumulates $\Delta t \varepsilon/k$ — the eddy-turnover clock"
findings.contradicts: PAGE: api / SimulationRun and observables_cache — turnover time = k/ε; PAGE: api / Forcing — t_ℓ = 2k/3ε = u'²/ε. Axis: the definition of the eddy-turnover time
findings.description: Both are conventional, but one name carries two numbers, and they meet in practice: `min_turnovers`/`window_turnovers` are counted on the k/ε clock while the controller's settling time t_ℓ/G is set on the u'²/ε one, so "5 turnovers of warm-up" and "settling time t_ℓ" differ by 1.5×.
findings.resolution_hint: Fix the convention once in notation.md; if the controller's choice is deliberate, say "= u'²/ε, not the k/ε clock".

findings.title: Pope's ℓ11 = 0.43 ℓ0 implies C_ε ≈ 0.79, against the package's own plateau of 0.5
locations: PAGE: api / phenomenology / Spectra, `large_scale_length` — "at Pope's high-Reynolds-number $\ell_{11} = 0.43\,\ell_{0}$"
PAGE: api / phenomenology / Scalings, `Sreenivasan1998` — "`asymptote = 0.5`" … "a constant of order $0.5$"
PAGE: api / phenomenology / Scalings, `Li2008` — "whose high-Reynolds-number plateau $C_\varepsilon \approx 0.5$"
findings.contradicts: PAGE: api / phenomenology / Scalings — "$C_\varepsilon \approx 0.5$" — axis: the value of the normalized dissipation constant (0.5 vs the 0.79 implied by 0.43 through the page's own identity)
findings.description: The identity ℓ11/ℓ0 = C_ε (2/3)^{3/2} is correct and both quoted numbers are defensible in their own sources, but the docstring places them side by side without saying the second IS a third value of the same constant. A reader taking Sreenivasan1998 as the package's C_ε and Pope's 0.43 as its high-Re limit gets two incompatible numbers.
findings.resolution_hint: Append "(i.e. C_ε ≈ 0.79 in this identity)" to the 0.43 clause.

findings.title: 1/(D κ_min²) is a box-scale diffusive bound, not a "resolution bound"
locations: PAGE: api / SimulationRun, `Simulation` `max_dt` — "a resolution bound $1/(D\kappa_{\min}^{2})$ built from the run's own diffusivity and box"
PAGE: api / SimulationRun, `advance!` — "the resolution bound the box and its diffusivity impose"
PAGE: api / SimulationDomain, `max_wavenumber` — "the resolution criterion $\kappa_{\max}\eta$"
findings.contradicts: PAGE: api / SimulationDomain — "the resolution criterion $\kappa_{\max}\eta$" — axis: "resolution" as the smallest resolved scale vs a bound built from κ_min, the largest
findings.description: The formula matches its stated job — exp(−Dκ²Δt) annihilates even the gravest mode once Δt ≳ 1/(Dκ_min²), which stops a decaying run's step running away — but that is a largest-eddy diffusive bound. Naming it "resolution" invites the reader to type it as a grid-scale constraint and to expect κ_max in it.
findings.resolution_hint: Call it the box-scale (gravest-mode) diffusive bound.

findings.title: The longitudinal integral scale wears two glyphs, L11 and ℓ11
locations: PAGE: notation, Derived scales — "$L_{11}$ | longitudinal (parallel) integral length scale"
PAGE: notation, Derived scales — "$\ell$ | the length a large-scale roll-off is evaluated against ($\ell_{11}$, or Pope's $\ell_0$…)"
PAGE: api / phenomenology / Spectra, `large_scale_length` — "the longitudinal integral scale $L_{11}$" … "related by $\ell_{11}/\ell_{0}$"
findings.contradicts: PAGE: notation — "$L_{11}$" vs "$\ell_{11}$" for one quantity — axis: one symbol per concept
findings.description: The same length appears as L11 and as ℓ11 inside a single docstring and inside the glossary table whose stated job is one-symbol-one-concept.
findings.resolution_hint: Keep L11 for the scale; reserve ℓ for "the length this roll-off was fitted against", writing ℓ = L11 where they coincide.

findings.title: The glossary gives E_φ(κ) no code object, though `spectrum` evaluates it
locations: PAGE: notation, Diagnostics — "$E_\varphi(\kappa)$ | the scalar-variance spectrum … | —"
PAGE: api / phenomenology / Phenomenology, `spectrum` — "or the scalar spectrum $E_\varphi(\kappa)$ for a `ScalarSpectrum`"
findings.contradicts: PAGE: notation — the same table binds E(κ) to `spectrum` but leaves E_φ(κ) unbound — axis: whether the symbol has a code home
findings.description: The dash reads as "not built", yet one generic serves both spectra and `ObukhovCorrsin1949` is shipped; `random_scalar_spectral!`'s `initial_spectrum` keyword also takes a κ ↦ E_φ(κ) target, so the symbol has two live code homes.
findings.resolution_hint: Fill the Code cell with `spectrum` (ScalarSpectrum) and cross-reference the seeder keyword.

findings.title: The cache's mid-step counterexample names only k; the default forcing also forms ε every stage
locations: PAGE: observables_cache, §1.2 — "no component of the iteration performs that reduction for the cache"
PAGE: observables_cache, §2.4 table — "(a constant-energy forcing forms $k$ mid-step and discards it)"
PAGE: architecture, §7 — "$\langle f, \lvert\boldsymbol{\kappa}\rvert^{2} f\rangle$ for the dissipation it replaces" (three per-stage reductions)
findings.contradicts: PAGE: architecture, §7 — the default run reduces for the dissipation at every stage — axis: whether any component of an iteration forms ε
findings.description: The conclusion (ε is not cached) survives — the stage value fails the survival test just as k does — but the stated reason, that no component performs the reduction, is false for the default configuration, and the qualification that rescues it is written for k alone. `add_forcing_source!`'s "three per stage for VarianceController" is the third witness.
findings.resolution_hint: Extend the §1.2/§2.4 counterexample sentence to ε and the band variance.

findings.title: VarianceController alone has no domain-taking form and is missing from the deferred-forcing list
locations: PAGE: api / Forcing, `VarianceController` — "`VarianceController(; target, gain = 1, turnover_time = nothing, …)`" with a "`band` — the band-pass kernel, lazy" field
PAGE: api / Forcing, `DeferredForcing` — the operator-free list gives only `Linear`, `ConstantPower`, `VarianceRescaling`
findings.contradicts: PAGE: api / Forcing, `DeferredForcing` — every other band forcing has a domain-taking constructor plus an operator-free twin — axis: the module's two-form construction convention
findings.description: ConstantPower's band kernel is documented as lazy too, yet it still takes `domain`. The reader cannot tell whether `VarianceController(; target = 1.5)` yields a concrete forcing or a `DeferredForcing` — which matters because it is the front door's default and `FlowConditions` accepts either kind.
findings.resolution_hint: State in the docstring why this one needs no domain and which kind of object it returns.

findings.title: The ObservablesCache signature omits history_depth, which its own Arguments document
locations: PAGE: api / Cache, `ObservablesCache` — "`ObservablesCache(domain; scalar = false, particle_velocities = nothing)`"
PAGE: api / Cache, same docstring — "`history_depth = 1` — how many Lagrangian samples the run must be able to look back over"
findings.contradicts: PAGE: api / Cache — the shown constructor against its own argument list — axis: which keywords the constructor takes
findings.description: The Fields section then documents `particle_velocity_history`, `sample_steps` and `history_filled`, which exist only because of that keyword, and the observables_cache §3.1 example also builds a cache without it. A reader wiring an AdamsBashforth run by hand cannot size the history from the signature.
findings.resolution_hint: Add `history_depth = 1` to the displayed signature.

findings.title: Two CatmullRom trajectory floors that cannot both hold under the stated Δx^{d+1} law
locations: PAGE: decisions, (2026-08) second trajectory scheme — "`CatmullRom` ($C^1$, degree 2) floors at $1.2\times10^{-5}$" (frozen ABC flow, $64^3$)
PAGE: api / Particles, `EndpointHeun` — "at $N = 128$, floor $1\times10^{-5}$ against time error $6\times10^{-5}$"
findings.contradicts: PAGE: api / Particles — floor ≈1e-5 at N=128 vs 1.2e-5 at N=64 — axis: the same interpolant's error floor under the docs' own "falls as Δx^{d+1}" scaling (a factor 8 apart)
findings.description: The two experiments differ (frozen ABC flow vs "a band-limited field"), so this need not be an error — but as rendered the reader sees one quantity, two grids, one number, and a scaling law the pair violates.
findings.resolution_hint: Name the test field beside each number, or quote both at one N.

findings.title: E_φ(κ) is described as "summing", though it is a density like E(κ)
locations: PAGE: notation, Diagnostics — "$E_\varphi(\kappa)$ | the scalar-variance spectrum, summing to $\langle\varphi^{2}\rangle$"
PAGE: notation, Diagnostics — "$E(\kappa)$ | … as a density per unit wavenumber … $k = \int_0^\infty E(\kappa)\,\mathrm{d}\kappa$"; "$E_n$ … so $k = \sum_n E_n$"
findings.contradicts: PAGE: notation — the table's own discriminator is that a density integrates and a shell set sums — axis: density vs per-shell quantity
findings.description: E_φ(κ) carries a continuous argument and is evaluated by `spectrum`, so it integrates; "summing" types it as the measured E_n kind — the very density-vs-shell-energy conflation the package treats as a guarded category error elsewhere.
findings.resolution_hint: Write "integrating to ⟨φ²⟩".

findings.title: `VarianceController`: the "marginal law" is quoted with the wrong denominator (k, not k_f)
locations: PAGE: api / Forcing, `VarianceController`: "The rate is the marginal law $A = \varepsilon/2k$ plus a proportional restoring term" — then displays $A = \frac{\varepsilon(t) - G[k(t)-k_\infty]/t_\ell}{2k_f(t)}$
PAGE: api / Forcing, same docstring: "The two variances there are not interchangeable: $k$ is the whole field's … and $k_f$ the forced band's"
PAGE: decisions, §References (Bassenne et al. 2016): "the marginal law $A = \varepsilon/2k$ plus a proportional restoring term"
findings.contradicts: PAGE: api / Forcing, `VarianceController` display formula — denominator $2k_f(t)$ — versus the prose's $2k$; axis: which variance normalizes the rate.
findings.description: The lead-in sentence and the §References gloss write the marginal law with the whole-field k in the denominator; the displayed formula (and the physics) need the band variance k_f. Only 2Ak_f equals the injected power, which is what makes the next claim, dk/dt = -G(k-k_inf)/t_l "exactly", true. Decision 58's own postscript records that swapping these two nearly shipped wrong physics and calls it a category error; the prose still carries the swapped form on two surfaces.
findings.resolution_hint: Write "the marginal law $A = \varepsilon/2k_f$" in both places, or gloss it as ε over twice the forced band's variance.

findings.title: Two different "eddy-turnover times" in one corpus — k/ε and 2k/3ε
locations: PAGE: api / Forcing, `VarianceController`: "the large-eddy turnover time $t_\ell$. When omitted it is taken as $2k_\infty/3\varepsilon_\infty$"
PAGE: api / SimulationRun, `StationarityCriterion`: "which normalizes the eddy-turnover clock $\Delta t \varepsilon/k$ it accumulates"
PAGE: observables_cache §1.3: "a budget in turnovers … accumulates $\Delta t \varepsilon/k$ — the eddy-turnover clock" (also ARCHITECTURE §4.7, api / Observables)
findings.contradicts: PAGE: api / Forcing $t_\ell = 2k/3\varepsilon$ versus PAGE: api / SimulationRun's clock $\Delta t\,\varepsilon/k$, i.e. turnover $= k/\varepsilon$; axis: the numerical value of one named timescale (factor 3/2).
findings.description: Both are dimensionally times, but they are not the same time. A user reading `min_turnovers = 5` (clock units ε/k) and then setting `gain` / `turnover_time` against "the large-eddy turnover time" is working in units that differ by 50%. Nothing on either surface flags the difference, and the controller's settling time t_l/G is quoted in the second convention while warmup!'s budget is quoted in the first.
findings.resolution_hint: Name the controller's parameter for its own convention (u'^2/ε = two-thirds of the k/ε turnover the run's clock counts), or align the two.

findings.title: "Four strategies are provided", then five are listed
locations: PAGE: architecture §4.4: "Four strategies are provided. `NoForcing` … `Linear` … `ConstantPower` … `VarianceController` … `VarianceRescaling`"
PAGE: Home, Work in progress: "the forcing menu `NoForcing`, `Linear`, `ConstantPower`, `VarianceController` (the default), and `VarianceRescaling`"
findings.contradicts: PAGE: architecture §4.4's count "Four" against the five names the same paragraph enumerates, and against the Home page's five-item menu.
findings.description: The sentence opens with a count of four and enumerates five strategies. The later clause in the same paragraph — "because these four methods are written through tensor-order-generic field operators" — is correct if NoForcing is excluded, which suggests the opening count was never updated when VarianceController was added (decision 58). The API and Home pages both list five.
findings.resolution_hint: "Five strategies are provided" (or "Four driving strategies, plus `NoForcing`").

findings.title: `L` is the box side everywhere except `ModelSpectrum`, where it names the roll-off length
locations: PAGE: api / phenomenology / Spectra, `ModelSpectrum`: "reads $\varepsilon$ and the roll-off's own length $L$ … $L_{11}$ for most forms, $k^{3/2}/\varepsilon$ for Pope's"
PAGE: api / phenomenology / Spectra, `LargeScaleFactor`: "with $\ell$ the length that form's own coefficient was fitted against, not the box side $L$"
PAGE: notation, Numerics: "$L$ | box side ($\Omega = [0,L)^3$) | side_length"
findings.contradicts: PAGE: api / phenomenology / Spectra `ModelSpectrum` binds $L$ to the roll-off length; `LargeScaleFactor` and the notation glossary bind $L$ to the box side and reserve $\ell$; axis: which length the glyph L denotes.
findings.description: The ModelSpectrum formula itself writes f_L(κℓ), so the prose one line below contradicts its own display; the same page's `large_scale_factor(f, κL)` names the argument κL where its text says κℓ. Since Δκ = 2π/L and the Li2008 group k/(Lε)^{2/3} both use L as the box side, the collision is load-bearing: a reader could substitute the box side into a roll-off fitted at L₁₁ or k^{3/2}/ε.
findings.resolution_hint: Use ℓ in the ModelSpectrum prose and rename the `κL` argument to `κℓ`.

findings.title: The scalar spectrum is a density, but the glossary says it "sums to" the variance
locations: PAGE: notation, Diagnostics: "$E_\varphi(\kappa)$ | the scalar-variance spectrum, summing to $\langle\varphi^{2}\rangle$"
PAGE: notation, Diagnostics (adjacent row): "$E(\kappa)$ | the energy spectrum as a density per unit wavenumber … $k = \int_0^\infty E(\kappa)\,\mathrm{d}\kappa$ (dimensions $L^3T^{-2}$)"
PAGE: api / phenomenology / Spectra, `ScalarSpectrum`: "parametrizations of $E_\varphi(\kappa)$, the density in wavenumber of the scalar variance"
findings.contradicts: PAGE: notation — "summing to" (the per-shell $E_n$ verb one row below) applied to $E_\varphi(\kappa)$, which the adjacent $E(\kappa)$ row and the Spectra page integrate; axis: per-shell energy vs spectral density.
findings.description: This is the exact per-shell-versus-density distinction the docs police elsewhere (decision 19, `energy_spectrum`, `integral_scale`). The E_φ row is the only spectrum entry that uses the sum verb for a density, and it is also the only one carrying no dimensions, so a reader has nothing to check the convention against.
findings.resolution_hint: "integrating to ⟨φ²⟩: ⟨φ²⟩ = ∫₀^∞ E_φ(κ) dκ (dimensions [φ]²L)".

findings.title: "A resolution bound 1/(Dκ_min²)" is built from the lowest wavenumber
locations: PAGE: api / SimulationRun, `Simulation`, `max_dt`: "a resolution bound $1/(D\kappa_{\min}^{2})$ built from the run's own diffusivity and box"
PAGE: api / SimulationDomain, `max_wavenumber`: "the resolution criterion $\kappa_{\max}\eta$"
findings.contradicts: PAGE: api / SimulationRun binds "resolution" to $\kappa_{\min}$; PAGE: api / SimulationDomain (and the `κ_max_η` keyword throughout) binds it to $\kappa_{\max}$; axis: which end of the spectrum "resolution" refers to.
findings.description: The quantity is dimensionally a time and κ_min is clearly intended — κ_max would reinstate the diffusive stability limit decision 1 exists to remove. But 1/(Dκ_min²) measures the largest-scale diffusive time, i.e. the step past which the integrating factor damps even the gravest mode; calling it a "resolution" bound points the reader at the opposite end of the spectrum from the word's meaning everywhere else in the docs.
findings.resolution_hint: "a diffusive-time bound 1/(Dκ_min²) on the gravest mode".

findings.title: The interpolation floor does not follow the Δx^{d+1} scaling the same docstring asserts
locations: PAGE: api / Particles, `EndpointHeun`: "a degree-$d$ interpolant's trajectory floor falls as $\Delta x^{d+1}$ … (at $N = 128$, floor $1\times10^{-5}$ …)"
PAGE: decisions (2026-08, AdamsBashforth): "Measured on a frozen ABC flow at $64^3$, $T = 1$: `CatmullRom` ($C^1$, degree 2) floors at $1.2\times10^{-5}$"
findings.contradicts: PAGE: api / Particles gives the CatmullRom floor as 1e-5 at N=128; PAGE: decisions gives 1.2e-5 at N=64 — a factor 1.2 where the stated Δx^{d+1}=Δx³ law demands 8; axis: the grid scaling of the interpolation error floor.
findings.description: Two measurements of the same interpolant's trajectory-error floor, one grid doubling apart, differ by 20% while the stated scaling law demands 8x. Either they come from different test problems (a frozen ABC flow versus "a band-limited field") and the docs should say so, or one is stale. As written, a reader who takes the scaling law and the N=64 number to predict the N=128 floor lands an order of magnitude away from the value printed elsewhere.
findings.resolution_hint: State the test problem beside each number, or re-measure one on the other's setup.

findings.title: The IFRK2 register count is justified by an assembly register `allocate_buffers` never gives it
locations: PAGE: architecture §4.5: "three spectral registers per field against the low-storage scheme's two, counting the same way on both sides: the scheme's own registers plus the dealiasing seam's assembly register"
PAGE: api / Propagator, `allocate_buffers`: "`IFLowStorageRK3` allocates `stage1` and `nonlinear`; `IFRK2` allocates `stage1`, `stage2`, and `velocity_predictor_spectral`"
PAGE: api / Propagator, `IntegratorBuffers`: "`nonlinear` — the assembled right-hand side; `IFLowStorageRK3` only, else `nothing`"
findings.contradicts: PAGE: architecture §4.5's decomposition "own registers + one assembly register" against PAGE: api / Propagator, where only `IFLowStorageRK3` owns an assembly register; axis: how the two register counts are decomposed.
findings.description: The totals (2 and 3) match the allocator, but the stated decomposition does not: IFRK2 has no `nonlinear` register at all, so its three are three scheme registers and zero assembly registers. The sentence is offered precisely as the guarantee that the two schemes are counted alike, which is what makes the mismatch worth fixing rather than ignoring.
findings.resolution_hint: Drop the "plus the assembly register" clause and say the counts are total spectral registers per field.

findings.title: The skewness episode is not "half again" the resident set the cache page reports
locations: PAGE: decisions (2026-07, the memory audit): "the velocity-derivative skewness $\approx 19.6$ — the dominant episode, about half again the default resident set"
PAGE: observables_cache §1.4: "a velocity-only run … carries six vector-shaped fields … about 2.3 GiB at $256^{3}$ in double precision"
findings.contradicts: PAGE: decisions claims a 1.5x ratio; PAGE: observables_cache's 2.3 GiB resident set makes 19.6 units of N³ reals (2.45 GiB) about 1.07x; axis: the size ratio of the transient episode to the resident set.
findings.description: Episodes are frozen "in units of N³ reals"; one unit is 128 MiB at 256³ in double precision, so 19.6 units ≈ 2.45 GiB against the page's 2.3 GiB working set. The current `derivative_skewness` docstring's weaker claim — "larger than the resident working set" — fits those numbers; the decision-log ratio does not. Low confidence because the log is append-only history and the resident set has shrunk twice (decisions 40, 41), though the pre-shrink ≈3.8 GiB does not fit "half again" either.
findings.resolution_hint: Either restate the ratio against the figure that was current, or drop the comparative and keep the absolute 19.6.

findings.title: `particles_modified!` contradicts itself in adjacent sentences
locations: PAGE: api / Cache, `particles_modified!`: "The run's own tracer advance is not such a change and keeps its history."
PAGE: api / Cache, `particles_modified!`, next sentence: "the run layer announces its own tracer advance (`advect!` followed by `record_particle_velocities!`, both inside `advance!`)"
findings.contradicts: Same docstring, one sentence later — axis: is the run's own tracer advance an announced change or not? "is not such a change" vs "the run layer announces its own tracer advance".
findings.description: Sentence one says the run's own advance is not the kind of change this verb announces; sentence two says the run layer does announce its own advance. A hand-run-loop reader cannot decide whether an in-loop push needs the call. The likely truth — the run layer bumps the particles epoch without discarding history — is exactly what the words deny. Failed PARAPHRASE: the two cannot both be restated as true.
findings.resolution_hint: REWRITE: separate "advances the epoch" from "announces an out-of-band change".

findings.title: Garbled field description on `ResolvedGenerator`
locations: PAGE: api / Generator, `ResolvedGenerator` → Fields: "the `û` whose displaced velocity `phase_shift.u_shifted` holds displaced velocity, left fresh by `velocity_rhs!`"
findings.description: The clause cannot be paraphrased: "the `û` whose displaced velocity … holds displaced velocity" repeats the noun phrase and leaves the relative clause without a predicate. A reader cannot tell whether the field stores a `û`, a freshness marker, or a buffer. Failed PARAPHRASE.
findings.resolution_hint: REWRITE, e.g. "the `û` the displaced velocity in `phase_shift.u_shifted` was recovered from".

findings.title: Subjectless sentence in `max_wavenumber`
locations: PAGE: api / SimulationDomain, `max_wavenumber`: "For the two sharp strategies sits strictly below the grid Nyquist $\tfrac{N}{2}\tfrac{2\pi}{L}$ — they zero the modes above it each step."
findings.description: The sentence has no subject; the reader must reconstruct "it" (the cutoff) from the previous sentence. It reads as a copy-edit casualty and stops a first-pass read. Failed LOAD-BEARING SUBJECT.
findings.resolution_hint: REWRITE: "For the two sharp strategies the cutoff sits strictly below …".

findings.title: `prepare!` stacks two parentheticals back to back
locations: PAGE: api / Generator, `prepare!`: "arm the per-mode linear forcing rates (fill them, so the factor verbs return them instead of `nothing`) (its `set_forcing_rate!` hook, written into the generator's rate arrays)"
findings.description: One ~70-word sentence carrying four clauses and three parentheticals, two of them adjacent with no connective and both glossing the same verb. The reader holds "advance … and arm …" open across 40 words before the arguments arrive. Failed DELETE TEST on the second parenthesis (the hook name belongs in the first) and LOAD-BEARING SUBJECT.
findings.resolution_hint: REWRITE: merge the two parentheses or split into two sentences.

findings.title: `StationarityCriterion`: a 90-word sentence with a 40-word aside inside it
locations: PAGE: api / SimulationRun, `StationarityCriterion`: "At each iteration it measures the dissipation $\varepsilon$ — … — and the kinetic energy $k$, which normalizes the eddy-turnover clock … and tests flatness over a trailing window"
findings.description: About 90 words and six clauses. The em-dash aside (why $k$ is not gated on) sits between the two objects of "measures", so "and the kinetic energy $k$" first reads as a new subject; the third verb "tests" must then be re-attached to "it" over 60 words of intervening text. Failed the ~40-word / 3-clause limit.
findings.resolution_hint: REWRITE as three sentences: what it measures, what it tests, why $k$ is excluded.

findings.title: Front-page quick start: "that value" has no antecedent
locations: PAGE: Home, "Quick start": "warmup!(sim)   # spin up to statistical stationarity … (the default forcing drives k to that value — see VarianceController before measuring k itself)"
findings.description: No value is named anywhere in the snippet — the only prior comments concern the grid and $\nu$. The reader meets a demonstrative pointing at nothing in the package's first code example. "see VarianceController before measuring k itself" then issues an instruction without saying what would be learned there. Failed PARAPHRASE (ambiguous pronoun).
findings.resolution_hint: REWRITE: name the value ("drives $k$ to the default `kinetic_energy = 1.5`").

findings.title: `initial_spectrum` states the assumed integral scale twice in one sentence
locations: PAGE: api / SimulationRun, `Simulation` → Arguments, `initial_spectrum`: "so its integral scale is `1/envelope_wavenumber` rather than the $L_{11}$ the seeded field will have"
PAGE: api / SimulationRun, same sentence ~40 words later: "and the integral scale as `1/envelope_wavenumber`"
findings.description: One ~85-word sentence with five clauses says the assumed integral scale is `1/envelope_wavenumber`, then repeats it as the last item of a four-item list inside the same sentence. The repetition makes a reader hunt for a distinction that is not there. Failed DELETE TEST on the second occurrence.
findings.resolution_hint: CUT the repeat and split the sentence at the colon.

findings.title: `recommended_cfl` explains a scaling one paragraph before stating it
locations: PAGE: api / Propagator, `recommended_cfl`: "The same $1/\kappa_{\max}$ scaling is applied to both schemes' bases, including `IFRK2`'s empirical one"
PAGE: api / Propagator, `recommended_cfl`, next paragraph: "It scales that base by the domain's dealiasing … $C_{\mathrm{CFL}} \propto 1/\kappa_{\max}$."
findings.description: The caveat about the $1/\kappa_{\max}$ scaling is printed before the sentence that introduces the scaling. "The same … scaling" refers forward to text the reader has not met, and the later paragraph's opening "It" must reach back past the caveat for its antecedent. Failed LOAD-BEARING SUBJECT — mechanism stated before the thing it qualifies.
findings.resolution_hint: REWRITE: swap the two paragraphs.

findings.title: `deposit!`'s argument-order sentence cancels its own first clause
locations: PAGE: api / Propagator, `deposit!`: "The argument order is shared with `step!` — the cache leads because it is what this call mutates — unlike `step!`, whose leading `scheme` is a dispatch tag — and `state`, `domain`, `buffers` follow in the same order as there."
PAGE: api / Propagator, `step!`: "The leading argument differs from `deposit!`'s in kind, and it is worth knowing which"
findings.contradicts: Within the one `deposit!` sentence — axis: is the argument order the same as `step!`'s or not? "shared with `step!`" vs "unlike `step!`".
findings.description: Three em-dash asides in one sentence, the second cancelling the first clause, leaving the reader unsure whether the orders agree. The same comparison is then made a second time from the other side in `step!`, where "it is worth knowing which" says something matters without saying what it changes for the caller. Only the shared tail (`state, domain, buffers`) is load-bearing.
findings.resolution_hint: REWRITE one and CUT the other.

findings.title: "One piece of prior art is excluded by name" — and no name follows
locations: PAGE: architecture, §8 Lenses and prior art: "One piece of prior art is excluded by name."
PAGE: architecture, §8, same paragraph: "The direction of the GBG packages is to replace it entirely, because it was problematic"
findings.description: The sentence promises a name and the paragraph gives none — the object is identified only as "the previous generation of this work — kept privately, outside the package". A reader cannot check or reason about an unnamed thing, so six sentences arguing that nothing may be justified by continuity with it defend against a confusion this document cannot create. "because it was problematic" asserts nothing falsifiable. Failed NON-VACUITY and UNPROVOKED DEFENCE.
findings.resolution_hint: CUT to one sentence, or name the artifact.

findings.title: The glossary's "resolved" entry does not define "resolved"
locations: PAGE: notation, "Vocabulary": "resolved | in ResolvedFields and ResolvedGenerator, made concrete as one value. The numerical sense — a scale the grid resolves … — is the other reading, and the docs write it out in full wherever it is meant."
findings.description: "Made concrete as one value" is the meaning of reified, not of resolved; no ordinary reading of the word yields it. The entry then disambiguates against grid resolution — a reading it makes more likely, not less, by offering a definition matching neither the numerical sense nor the resolved/filtered axis the architecture page uses (`ResolvedGenerator` with `FilteredGenerator` "the eventual LES sibling"). Failed PARAPHRASE and UNPROVOKED DEFENCE.
findings.resolution_hint: REWRITE as the resolved/filtered axis, which is what the type names encode.

findings.title: `IFLowStorageRK3` denies two symbol collisions it alone introduces
locations: PAGE: api / Propagator, `IFLowStorageRK3`: "unrelated to the forcing rate $A(\boldsymbol{\kappa})$ of the `Forcing` page"
PAGE: api / Propagator, `IFLowStorageRK3`: "not the grid points $N$ of the rest of the documentation"
findings.description: Two defensive asides in one docstring, each naming a symbol from another page purely to deny it. Neither confusion is created here — the forcing rate never otherwise appears in this docstring — so both first introduce the reading they refuse. Struck, nothing is lost. Failed UNPROVOKED DEFENCE and DELETE TEST.
findings.resolution_hint: CUT both; a symbol clash is settled on the notation page.

findings.title: `fit` restates its own first sentence
locations: PAGE: api / phenomenology / Phenomenology, `fit`: "No methods are defined yet; it is the recorded extension point for fitting a run's own measurements to a parametrization."
findings.description: The trailing clause repeats the opening sentence ("the seam by which a run's own measurements become a parametrization sitting beside the literature") with the words re-ordered. Only "No methods are defined yet" carries new information. Failed DELETE TEST.
findings.resolution_hint: CUT the trailing clause.

findings.title: `DeferredForcing`'s example is introduced by editorial housekeeping
locations: PAGE: api / Forcing, `DeferredForcing` → Examples: "The two-form construction is the non-obvious part of this module, so the example lives here; the strategies themselves are built by the forms shown below."
findings.description: The first clause explains why the documentation is laid out as it is — a fact about the docs, not the code. The second points at "the forms shown below", where what follows is the example itself and then `# Fields`, so the reader looks for a list that is not there. Failed NON-VACUITY (first clause) and PARAPHRASE (second).
findings.resolution_hint: CUT.

findings.title: `max_dt`: a four-clause run-on closing on "stops that"
locations: PAGE: api / SimulationRun, `Simulation` → Arguments, `max_dt`: "The advective rule alone diverges as a decaying flow approaches rest — … — and it is the resolution bound that stops that, needing no constant from the caller."
findings.description: About 55 words across four clauses, with a 20-word em-dash aside separating subject from verb, closing on "stops that", whose referent is the aside rather than the main clause. The surrounding argument list is otherwise clear, which makes this the one sentence a reader stalls on.
findings.resolution_hint: REWRITE as two sentences.

findings.title: "An epoch is not an iteration number" is defended on four surfaces
locations: PAGE: api / Cache, module: "An epoch counts changes to the state, not advances of the run"
PAGE: notation, "Vocabulary": "Not an iteration number: an announced out-of-band mutation advances an epoch without advancing the clock."
PAGE: api / SimulationRun, `current_step`: "after two steps and one announced mutation the clock reads step 2 and the fields epoch reads 4"
PAGE: decisions: "after two steps and one announced mutation the clock reads step 2 and the fields epoch reads 4 — measured, not assumed"
findings.description: The same denial appears on four surfaces plus the `ObservablesCache` field list, twice with the identical worked example. At this density the repetition stops reading as clarification: a reader meeting it the fourth time learns nothing and begins to suspect the two really are confusable in the code. Failed DELETE TEST at three of the four sites.
findings.resolution_hint: CUT to one home (the `Cache` module docstring) plus the glossary line.

findings.title: `ScalingLaw`: a trailing modifier with nothing to modify
locations: PAGE: api / phenomenology / Scalings, `ScalingLaw`: "— here the normalized dissipation $C_\varepsilon$, the Kolmogorov constant $C_K$, and the box-normalized dissipation group $G$ — possibly Reynolds-number-dependent."
findings.description: Three em-dash asides in one sentence, the last a bare adjective phrase that could attach to $G$, to the list, or to "a pure number characterizing developed turbulence" 30 words earlier — and read as attaching to the nearest noun it sits oddly against "a pure number". Failed PARAPHRASE (dangling modifier).
findings.resolution_hint: REWRITE as its own sentence: "Each may carry a Reynolds-number trend."

findings.title: `restart!`'s closing clause is unparaphrasable
locations: PAGE: api / Particles, `restart!`: "a scheme carrying registers beyond that history is reached only this way"
findings.description: The sentence runs 45 words over three clauses, opens on "Its" (antecedent `particles_modified!`, two sentences back), and closes on a passive with no agent: the reader cannot tell what is "reached", by whom, or what goes wrong if the call is skipped. Failed PARAPHRASE on the final clause.
findings.resolution_hint: REWRITE the last clause: name the registers and the consequence of skipping the call.
